title: `FLOAT` and `DOUBLE` are IEEE 754 binary32 and binary64
verdict: `rounding: TIE_TO_EVEN` for `+ - * /`: plain C++ float and double operations
description: `FLOAT` (`FLOAT4`, `REAL`) is single precision and `DOUBLE` (`FLOAT8`) double precision, in practice IEEE 754 "to the extent that the underlying processor, operating system, and compiler support it". Addition, subtraction and multiplication are approximate on them, so each result is the operands' IEEE result, rounded to nearest with ties to even, the default IEEE mode. The docs name no other rounding mode and no setting that changes it.

`/` of two integers is float division (`5 / 2 = 2.5`) while `integer_division` is false (the default); `//` divides integers. `ieee_floating_point_ops` (default true) selects IEEE results (NaN, `±inf`) over errors or NULL for supported floating-point operations; it does not touch rounding.

The source confirms it (round 2): `+ - * /` on FLOAT and DOUBLE are the C++ operators on `float` and `double`, so a FLOAT operation rounds to binary32 once and is not computed in double. The result is the platform's IEEE arithmetic in its default rounding mode; DuckDB sets no other.
reference: `rounding: TIE_TO_EVEN` for `+ - × /` of doubles (exact, rounded once: docs/core-semantics.md D5, D31; the platform facts `duckdb-ieee-arith-*`). Lean refuses arithmetic on `FLOAT` values (duckdb-R12), so the fp32 rows matter only once binary32 is modelled.

evidence.note: Floating-Point Types: FLOAT and DOUBLE are usually implementations of IEEE 754 single and double precision; multiplication, addition and subtraction are only approximate on them
ieee_floating_point_ops (default true); integer_division (default false): whether / defaults to integer division
Division and Modulo Operators: / and // are equivalent when an operand is FLOAT or DOUBLE
+ on floating types binds GetScalarBinaryFunction<AddOperator> at the type's own width
/ of FLOAT and of DOUBLE: BindBinaryFloatingPoint<DivideOperator>

provenance.notes: Each operator has a `float` and a `double` specialisation that is the bare C++ operation; `ieee_floating_point_ops` only chooses whether `/` and `%` check for a zero divisor first (BindBinaryFloatingPoint).

evidence.note: CompareValues: numeric results are cast to the column type and compared with Value::ValuesAreEqual
ApproxEqual: NaN equals NaN, non-finite values compare exactly, finite ones within 1 %

provenance.notes: A FLOAT sum past 3.4e38 is inf, so FLOAT arithmetic rounds at binary32. Overflow to ±inf in both directions rules out TRUNCATE, FLOOR and CEILING, which give ±max there, and leaves the two round-to-nearest modes; no test pins a tie. The runner compares FLOAT and DOUBLE results within 1 % and counts NaN equal to NaN of either sign and `-0.0` equal to `0.0` (`test/sqlite/result_helper.cpp`, `ApproxEqual` in `src/common/types.cpp`); infinities, integers, booleans and strings compare exactly. So the rows stay at the source reading.
